newsitem.title: USA: Special prosecutor favored on fundraising - poll.
newsitem.headline: Special prosecutor favored on fundraising - poll.

text.p: A majority of Americans favours the appointment of a special prosecutor to investigate questionable fundraising by the Democratic Party, according to an ABC News poll released Tuesday.
Six in 10 said the campaign fund controversy required a full-scale federal investigation and 56 percent felt a special counsel, not the Justice Department, should do the investigating.
More than two-thirds of those surveyed said the case was an important one and 57 percent said they thought some of the contributions to the Democratic National Committee were illegal.

The poll was conducted by telephone Monday among a random national sample of 500 adults and has a margin of error of plus or minus five percentage points. The results were broadcast on the ABC News programme "Nightline."
Attorney General Janet Reno has rejected three congressional requests for an independent probe into allegations of possibly illegal campaign contributions to the DNC from foreign businessmen.

The Justice Department said all three requests failed to meet the law's requirement of "specific, credible evidence" that a person covered by the independent counsel act had committed a federal crime.

But Congress plans to go ahead with its own investigations. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said last week the Governmental Affairs Committee would proceed with an inquiry immediately after the new Congress was sworn in Jan. 7.
Other investigations into the affair that has embarrassed the White House and prompted the DNC to return about $1.5 million in "inappropriate" donations are getting under way in the House.
